 Patrick Stewart’s cause of death revealed after actor died at 86 
 By 
 Antoinette Bueno 
 Published 
 Oct. 29, 2026, 4:08 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Patrick Stewart died after a battle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.
 In a statement from the late actor’s Instagram account Thursday, his family shared he died at his home in Los Angeles after a “brief and poignant journey” with the diseases.
 He was 86 years old.

 They also noted in the caption that In lieu of flowers, memorial contributions may be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.
 “He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement also reads. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
 According to the Mayo Clinic , Lewy body dementia causes a decline in mental abilities that gradually gets worse over time.
 Symptoms are similar to those with Parkinson’s Disease, and may include rigid muscles, slow movement, trouble walking and tremors.
 6

  It’s the second most common type of dementia after Alzheimer’s disease, for which there is no cure.
 In July, Stewart said there were fewer roles available to him at his age.
 “That being said, I still continue to receive interesting offers and I love being challenged by new work, like voicing a pig’s head in Riz Ahmed‘s brilliant new series ‘Bait,'” he told TV Insider. 
 He added, “I can’t imagine ever officially ‘retiring.” I’ll always and forever be an actor.”
 Stewart was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and for his role as Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” film series.

 Marvel Studios shared that they were heartbroken over his death Thursday.
 “Stewart made his debut as Professor X in 2000’s ‘X-Men ,’  where he embodied the composure, class, and wisdom of the beloved telepathic mutant and mentor of the X-Men,” they said in a statement. “For more than 25 years, he brought a gravitas and profundity to the role, earning fans across the globe and helping to transform Super Hero storytelling forever.”
 “Sir Patrick Stewart leaves behind an indelible cultural footprint and legacy.”
 The British actor was also an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and had been a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company since the 1960s. 
 He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for his services to drama.
